title: Disassembly
overview: Remove the stator and rotor from the housing to access the drive pin.

steps.title: Locate the drive pin set plug
steps.description: Identify the set plug for the drive pin, which secures the connecting rod. The plug is located on the bottom of the housing and has a small indentation.

steps.title: Remove the hold down plug
steps.description: Remove the hold down plug from the drive pin using an alignment tool. This will expose the drive pin. Check that the plug is removed completely and not damaged.

steps.title: Remove the drive pin
steps.description: Use a leveraged pipe for the pipe wrench to remove the drive pin from the housing. The pin should be easily removable at this point.

steps.title: Remove the cap screws
steps.description: Remove the four cap screws with a 3-8 drive, three-quarter inch socket. Check that all screws are removed and not damaged.

steps.title: Mark the position of the cap
steps.description: Mark the position of the cap on both sides to ensure it is properly aligned during reassembly. This will prevent cross-threading or misalignment.

steps.title: Remove the stator and rotor
steps.description: Use a large pipe wrench to remove the stator and rotor from the housing assembly. Use a leverage bar pipe to assist with removal, if necessary.

steps.title: Set the stator and rotor aside
steps.description: Slide the stator and rotor out of the housing assembly using a helper. Set them aside on the floor to prevent damage or cross-contamination.

steps.title: Inspect the connecting rod washer
steps.description: Check the seal on the end of the connecting rod for proper installation and condition. The washer should be in good condition and properly seated.

steps.title: Verify the connecting rod washer is in place
steps.description: Ensure the connecting rod washer is properly seated on the end of the connecting rod. If damaged or missing, replace it immediately to prevent corrosion.

steps.title: Clean and inspect the housing assembly
steps.description: Inspect the housing assembly for any signs of damage, wear, or corrosion. Clean the area as needed before reassembly.
